by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here




I wrote a 

piece

 in September about the roots of the word “anarchy” and wondered “if the deep meaning of anarchy is, in fact, our human struggle against vitaphobic, authoritarian and psychopathic forces known as archons”. [1]




The Swedish writer 

Per Shapiro

 [2] subsequently sent me a pdf of a 2014 essay by John Lamb Lash on the archons of gnostic tradition in which he likewise presents anarchy as the antidote to their domination.




In ‘

The True Anarchy of Life on Earth

‘ Lash writes of “the scheme of the Archon mind-parasites to insinuate themselves into human reality and take it over, making humans become like them, robotic, slavish, incapable of intention, discovery, or novelty”. [3]




He stresses: “To fall under the spell of the Authorities is to concede power to their false magic: under the power of deception, we deceive ourselves about what power really is and lose all sense of our own power”. [4]




In order to resist this rule we need to embrace anarchy in the 

real

 [5] sense of the word: “We cannot realize our true humanity without beating the Authorities. There is more than one way to do so, but the central and decisive way is to choose anarchy in defiance of 

any

 authority that does not demonstrate benevolence toward life in all forms… Even the word carries the essential message: an-arch, ‘against authority, against archons'”. [6]










Lash equates the gnostic version of the archons with “globalist predators and serial killers, who are one and the same breed of conniving, murderous deviants”. [7]




Wondering what makes them so different from us, and how they achieve their deception and control, he suggests: “Archons and their human counterparts gain control over humanity through a particular ‘seizure’ that operates in the back of the brain and in the field of peripheral vision simultaneously” – this involves the “reptilian brain 

in its deviant or exaggerated mode

“. [8]




“In large measure, the quasi-magical or occult power attributed to globalist perpetrators is a hoax, operating under the Wizard of Oz effect. Note that to enforce their presumed magical powers, the perpetrators need to exert enormous continual efforts of two kinds: brainwashing through the media, and threat of force through the military.




“Without a constant dual-barreled barrage, requiring the complicity of human beings to suppress and deceive their fellow creatures, their vaunted magic would quickly fade and dissipate…




“In reality, the NEWOs [New World Order psychopaths] can only sustain the 

illusion

 of magical supremacy as long as they suppress and deviate human potential, where the true magic abides: that is, 

in our species’ innate capacity for interactive magic with the animating powers of the planetary goddess

. Unless the NEWOs can suppress 

that

 capacity in a brutal manner all the time, it will naturally and spontaneously assert itself”. [9]










This is how I also see anarchy – as the life force within humankind, constantly surging forth in each new generation and trying to break out of the industrial-imperial prison in which we have been locked up for so long.




Of course, the system has to lie about what anarchy is, as Lash sets out. “The supreme moral illusion confronting humanity operates like this: those who falsely assume authority over others demand obedience to their commands 

on the claim that disobedience would result in social chaos and anarchy

.




“They claim to preserve social and moral order by rules and constraints imposed and maintained by sheer brutal force. The self-assumed authorities propagate the belief that human beings, left to their own impulses, would produce a world of disorder, conflict, and chaos.




“We are all potential terrorists in the mind of the Authorities. In our natural state of freedom and autonomy, we are dangerous to ourselves and must be curbed, leashed, and protected by a higher power. In short, the self-declared authorities claim to save humanity from the chaotic or anarchistic tendencies of human nature”. [10]




But in fact, as anarchists are always pointing out, 

normal

 human nature is not the same as that of the globalist deviants. Lash states: “The evidence that people act from innate goodness, without having to be told to do so, is strong enough, and it stands in contrast to guilt-driven action which has to be contrived and enforced from without – by threat of eternal damnation, for instance”. [11]




He is on similar territory in his analysis to Andrew M. Lobaczewski in his book 

Political Ponerology: A science on the nature of evil adjusted for political purposes

 which I wrote about in October 2025 in an essay entitled ‘

The psychopaths in power

‘. [12]










The Polish author says of such people: “They become experts in our weaknesses and sometimes effect heartless experiments. The suffering and injustice they cause inspire no guilt within them, since such reactions from others are simply a result of their being different and apply only to ‘those other’ people they perceive to be not quite conspecific”. [13]




And I was pleased to see that Lash recommends Lobaczewski’s work in his essay, explaining: “Derived from the Greek word 

poneria

 found in Gnostic writings, ponerology is the diagnosis and deconstruction of the causes and mechanisms of social evil.




“Lobaczewski uses the striking term 

pathocracy

 to describe the domination of a society by a faction of psychopathic members, estimated to be 4-5 percent of the population”. [14]




The great champion of life and humanity against the archons, in the gnostic tradition, is Sophia, the goddess of wisdom, to whom I dedicated a 

series of articles

 in 2024. [15]




The Nag Hammadi library (the “Gnostic Gospels”) consists of early Christian and gnostic texts discovered near the Upper Egyptian town of Nag Hammadi in 1945. There, in the 

Apocryphon of John

, Sophia declares of the archons: “The tree of their design is bitterness and its branches are darkened by death. Its leaves are hatred and deception, and its aroma reeks of evil (

poneria

)”. [16]










Lash writes: “Perhaps even the wisdom goddess herself did not anticipate how far the Archons would penetrate human reality and deviate the divine experiment she previsioned for the Anthropos.




“This might explain, in mythological terms, why it takes until the last minute before she catches the error and initiates her correction. 

On the Origin of the World

 presents a kind of prophetic warning pronounced by the wisdom goddess, suggesting a last-minute turnaround: ‘For at the consummation of your work, the entire defect that will have become visible in the light of truth will be abolished, and will be as if it never had been’.




“In this scenario, Sophia, before she morphs into the earth, foresees a moment when the Archontic powers will be defeated, 

the moment of the consummation of their works

. In other words, their defeat comes at the moment of extreme desperation when they complete their agenda, the eleventh hour”. [17]




I, for one, am very much looking forward to the day when humankind is inspired into magical action by the life-affirming force of anarchy and the psychopathic archons are finally thrown into what Lash describes as “the gravity well (abyss) of the inanimate planetary system”! [18]

I am sure you don’t need me to tell you that we are heading into a crucial period of history.

“Others suggested creating thousands of new places in prisons on the model of Nayib Bukele in El Salvador, of removing benefits from the trouble-makers’ families or of hardening the law against minors”.

He adds that the French railways, SNCF, cancelled trains to prevent some people from attending demos and those arriving by road and rail were subject to police checks.




 “In Paris, the army was mobilised to supervise the demonstrators, along with the brigade of regional intervention, the RAID (

Recherche, assistance, intervention, dissuasion

But in the face of all that, numbers on the protests across France did not drop away and the uprising is still going strong as I write!

Regarding those protests,

relates

The blog states: “Not only are grannies and wheelchair users terrorists for expressing opinions the government doesn’t like, but anyone who is nice to those grannies and wheelchair users is also a terrorist”.

Because ZIM has, indeed, stolen most of the world’s wealth and captured most of the world’s institutions, this threat is not something we are going to be able to see off through letter-writing, petitions or voting for the usual political puppets.




I think this is why,  in recent weeks, I have been returning to anarchism as a source of inspiration. It is not only the anarchist

3. 

Banned from Canada










by 

Keith McHenry




The salmon and turquoise glow illuminated the Taos Mountains outside the dining room window. Allan Antliff, professor of Art History and Visual Studies at the University of Victoria, glass artist Mary Shaffer, and I enjoyed dinner at her beautiful adobe home in Taos, New Mexico, one evening in 2017. Mary and Allan had just met in Marfa, Texas, during the former ghost town’s annual open studio exhibits.




Allan asked if I would be interested in having my archives at his university, and I accepted his offer. I spent several months organizing my documents in the manner he suggested, and once they were ready, I drove cases of legal documents, flyers, sketchbooks, newsletters, and personal planners up to British Columbia, crossing into Canada on the ferry in my G20 conversion van. This would be one of nearly 40 trips to Canada I had made since I settled my 25-to-life Three Strikes Felony case on February 16, 1995, in Judge Lucy McCabe’s San Francisco court. The criminal case started when I was attacked by Mayor Frank Jordan’s film commissioner, Nick Rommel, in a first-floor City Hall phone booth. The near-daily arrests for felony conspiracy to share food in violation of a court order had not stopped us from feeding the homeless, so it seems that the mayor thought sending me to prison for a quarter of a century might do the trick.




After I made my first delivery for the archives, I periodically shipped more materials, including original paintings and the 750,000-word manuscript of what would become my 150,000-word memoir, 

Soup Street.










I emailed Allan to let him know my first memoir would be published in May 2026 and that I was ready to come up to Victoria as promised. Allan responded, “I propose organizing a Big Celebration of Food Not Bombs at University of Victoria to showcase your Food Not Bombs collection in the Anarchist Archive, plus you can launch your book at the event.” He purchased a round-trip flight from San Francisco and emailed me a link to request a table at the Victoria Anarchist Bookfair. He warned me that some of the local activists were smearing me and to make sure my application focused on my books. These were the same smears that had been used to cancel my presentation at the fifth anniversary of the founding of Food Not Bombs in Waltham, Massachusetts, suggesting there is an intelligence agency effort to silence anarchists who question obedience to government policies.




I was excited to speak at the dedication of the Food Not Bombs archives on Monday, September 21, 2026, and present my latest title, 

Soup Street,

 at the Victoria Anarchist Bookfair.




When I landed at Vancouver International Airport, all went well until I was stopped by Canadian Border and Customs. I have entered Canada at least 40 times since 1995. Each time I entered, I would be questioned about my felony conviction in San Francisco for assault, battery, and strong-arm robbery. I would explain that I had been framed by Mayor Jordan in San Francisco’s campaign to stop Food Not Bombs from protesting war by feeding the hungry.










I would share that I had to plead out in a case in which I was attacked in a phone booth at San Francisco City Hall by the mayor’s film commissioner. As I was telling them about the events of January 4, 1994, I would open a copy of one of my books, such as 

Hungry for Peace,

 and show them the photos of the riot police guarding the food from the homeless at Golden Gate Park. I would tell the story of the arrest, explaining that I was wearing a chef’s coat and a puffy chef’s hat and had been holding a sign saying “Viva Zapatista, No NAFTA” while waiting for the rest of the food to be delivered for that noon’s meal. “Some guy crossed over the street from City Hall and yelled at me.” The deranged man made a call on his flip phone, and before long, a tow truck arrived and towed my truck and its load of bagels from my legal parking spot.




I described how I walked through the City Hall metal detectors to the closest payphone to call parking and traffic to locate my pickup. The guy I would later learn was Nick Rommel cornered me and started attacking me.




I would tell them that while on the call, I told the woman at towing, “I am sorry; someone is smashing against the phone booth, and I have to find another phone to call from.” That often drew a smile from the Canadian officials.




I continued by explaining that I went to a second-floor payphone and, after locating my truck, I headed down that beautiful cascade of stairs in the rotunda. As I was about halfway down the stairs, one of those in the mayor’s police detail called out, “Hey Keith, we want to speak with you.” I described how one of the officers had a little blue book, holding it up and saying I was being arrested under the new California Three Strikes law, suggesting the code was in the publication.




Most of the time, the Canadian border officials would laugh at the insanity of the conviction and wave me through. If they didn’t, I would drive to the next border crossing; I would repeat the story, and they would wave me through.










Not this time.




A tall, lanky officer directed me to place my suitcase and backpack on a long stainless steel counter. His partner removed all my things and spread them out.




I shared the story of my having been arrested for feeding the homeless and gave her a copy of the letter of invitation from the University of Victoria. I opened the books 

Hungry for Peace

 and 

Soup Street

 to show the photos of riot police guarding the food from the homeless, but the young customs official, Jessica Vung, was not interested and told me she had to go to a back room to check things out.




She returned, asked more questions, and went to the back office. When she returned, she asked if I had ever had any problems getting into Canada before. I replied that I am always questioned about this arrest, but I have always been let in. I told her about the time I was crossing over at Niagara, and an officer found two glass vials in my ashtray, unscrewed the cap on one of them, licked her finger, and tasted the powder. When the officer asked what it was, I told her that it was my friend Eric Weinberger’s ashes. The seven border officers searching my vehicle all stepped away from my van and let me into Canada.




While I was sitting and waiting for the border and customs officer to return from the back room, I got a text from Air Canada saying my flight to Victoria was boarding. The official came back and asked more questions. The next time she returned, she asked if I wanted any food or water and showed me a menu. I requested water, coffee, and their vegetarian sandwich without cheese. They also let me charge my phone. I called my girlfriend, Kathleen, in Santa Cruz to tell her what was happening. She called Allan to let him know that I still hadn’t made it through customs.




The officer was growing more sympathetic with each encounter. When she would return from the back office, I started to greet her with “Fantastic, so they are letting me in,” and she would smile, but there were others in the back room who had other ideas. Kathleen suggested I show them the letter from Amnesty International in which they would declare Food Not Bombs activists “prisoners of conscience” and call for our unconditional release if convicted. I found the document on my phone and showed it to them, but they didn’t seem too interested.










At one point, she asked me about the FBI and its interest in Food Not Bombs. I shared that according to a 2009 U.S. State Department lecture on C-SPAN comparing the people who share vegan meals in the parks with al-Qaeda and asking who was more dangerous, the Obama State Department official claimed that the people sharing vegan meals were more dangerous because they were friendly local community members who were advocating that our taxes should be “diverted from the military to fund healthcare, education and other social services.” He claimed that if Americans were to agree with the vegans, there wouldn’t be enough funding to fight al-Qaeda.




I ate the Tim Hortons sandwich with lettuce and a slice of tomato before she led me to the back room. That officer told me that under Canadian law, they couldn’t let me in because in Canada my “conviction” would be penal code —blah, blah, blah. She told me they would not charge me with a criminal violation of Canada’s immigration laws and would just send me back to the United States.




The officer placed two papers in front of me. One was “Allowed to Leave Canada,” and the other said “is a person who is a foreign national who has not been authorized to enter Canada and who in my opinion, is inadmissible pursuant to: Paragraph 36(1)(b) in that there are reasonable grounds to believe is a permanent resident or foreign national who is inadmissible on grounds of serious criminality for having been convicted of an offense outside Canada that, if committed in Canada would constitute an offense under Act of Parliament punishable by a maximum term of imprisonment of at least 10 years.”




Below that, in the section titled “This report is based on the following information,” item 4 stated “Sought entry on 2026/09/18 at Vancouver International Airport for the purpose of speaking at a presentation in Victoria.”




Item 5 read, “Was convicted on 1994-10-28 for Force?ADW Not Firearm:GBI Likely (245(A)(1)PC San Francisco.”




It is odd that they claimed I was convicted on October 28, 1994, since I pleaded out, getting credit for 500 days served in jail to avoid life in prison on February 16, 1995, and the only court appearance of mine in October 1994 was on Halloween. It was a very memorable court appearance because those who came to support me took Halloween candy set out at offices throughout the courthouse and shared the treats with the public to mock the law against sharing food that had placed me in this position.




The Notice of Transporter had the checkbox labeled “allowed to withdraw his/her application to enter under section 42IRPR” checked.




I signed the forms.










They had said that they had to put me on the first flight to the United States, which was leaving for Austin, Texas, at 2:00 a.m., because that was Canadian policy. I asked if Air Canada would fly me to San Francisco from Austin, but that was not possible. I would have to buy my own ticket home. Finally, they agreed to send me on the morning flight to San Francisco.




A security team directed me to remove all my belongings, including my wallet, phone, belt, shoes, and pain medication, and ordered me to stand against the wall with my hands spread out. They frisked me, checked under my hair, and placed me in a chilly holding cell with the lights blazing. I tried to sleep on the metal-ribbed bench, but it was impossible. It would turn out that this aggravated the back injury I had been seeking surgery for, and I suffered level-10 pain for the following two weeks.




The distant clanging of doors and muffled conversations filled me with the dread I remembered when locked up during my days in jail facing the Three Strikes sentence.




Finally, they opened the cell and told me to get dressed. A security woman took me to the ticket desk where papers had to be signed. After that, she led me through the TSA-style security check, then took me to U.S. Customs, where the officer asked why I was being removed. I said for feeding the hungry. After that brief interaction, the security officer walked me to the gate. Following a 30-minute wait, the security officer led me to the boarding agent.




While waiting to board, I spoke with another passenger who it turned out was headed to TrueNorth Health in Santa Rosa, California. I let her know I had done several water-only fasts at TrueNorth and found it very helpful. I shared that my first 23-day water-only fast cured me of 20 years of suffering from fibromyalgia. This seemed to give her hope that she could recover from her autoimmune illness. Sadly, after all the “coincidences” in my life that have turned out to be part of an intelligence operation, I worried this might also be the case, but so far there is no evidence of this, and it was likely one of the many non-state-sponsored events of serendipity that have blessed my life.




There were more papers signed at the gate. I boarded, and a white envelope was handed over to an Air Canada employee. I was tired and in so much pain that I found the flight exhausting.




When I was leaving the plane in San Francisco, an airline attendant handed me a white envelope with legal documents and my passport. I phoned Kathleen to let her know I had landed and headed for the area where Ubers do their pickups. A young man was standing outside his car and I asked if he was an Uber driver. He was, and he was willing to drive me home to Santa Cruz.










My girlfriend, Kathleen, had emailed my emergency contacts while I was in the holding cell. Among those who responded was my friend and one of my lawyers, Randy Baker, who had defended me against the attacks by the government in San Francisco and had filed the civil rights lawsuits that included documents in discovery that provided me with the September 27, 1988, wiretap memo by San Francisco Police Department commander Richard Holder that was used to justify the police beating I took outside the Presidio on October 15, 1988, during a protest against the U.S. war in El Salvador. This is the text of his response to Kathleen’s email.




“Keith is indeed an exemplary man. Few people have allowed themselves to be subjected to the scores — perhaps hundreds — of arrests, and numerous beat-ups that Keith has suffered in the cause of advocating for a society in which our abundant resources are devoted to human needs, rather than to unnecessary wars.




In the course of representing Keith and Food Not Bombs in the early 1990s a letter from the San Francisco D.A. to the San Francisco City Attorney that I obtained in discovery in one of Keith’s suits underscored that law enforcement was not the objective underlying the City’s relentless brutality towards Keith and Food Not Bombs. The letter told the City Attorney to stop the arrests, because his office would not prosecute the cases. Yet the arrests and police harassment continued.




Since Food Not Bombs’ dispensing of free bagels, miso soup and anarchist literature was not threatening public safety, and prosecution was off the table, it became rather difficult to conclude anything other than that the point of the City’s persecution of Food Not Bombs was to stop their highly visible and poignant representation of the insanity of our current system, attracting groups of largely unsheltered people standing in line for food in highly visible venues — along with the message that things didn’t have to be this way.




In light of the City’s clearly speech-suppressive objective underlying its relentless persecution of Keith and Food Not Bombs, I think it virtually unbelievable that the prosecution that resulted in Keith’s convictions cited by Canadian officials was not the result of the City’s presentation of a grossly misleading account of an incident, rather than any felonious conduct on Keith’s part.




Insofar as Canada has relied on those convictions in considering the appropriateness of Keith’s entry into the country, it is grossly mistaken. Canada can only benefit from his presence. The government needs to reconsider its decision to exclude him.”




“Randy Baker




Attorney at Law”










During this ordeal, I often thought of how lucky I was, thinking of all those people captured by ICE, often disappeared from their families and held in horrid conditions for weeks and months before being shipped off to countries with which they often have no connection. Stories like that have been shared by a young Food Not Bombs volunteer in Monterrey, Mexico, who had spent his life in San Antonio, only to be dropped off in a remote area of Mexico and forced to search for his friends who had come to the border to meet him.

title: Raising ourselves from the lowness of modernity
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here




Ernst Friedrich Schumacher (1911-1977)

 is best remembered for his 1973 book 

Small is Beautiful: A Study of Economics As If People Mattered

 and its message that “infinite growth in a finite environment is an obvious impossibility”. [1]




As the title of the book conveys, he saw it as important to restore a human scale to human self-organisation: “Centralisation is mainly an idea of order; decentralisation, one of freedom”. [2]




Schumacher’s attack on centralisation and economic growth went hand in hand with a broader assault on industrial society itself.




He noted in 

Small is Beautiful

 that “modern man has built a system of production that ravishes nature and a type of society that mutilates man”. [3]




As I explain in my 

profile

 of Schumacher on the organic radicals site, [4] he also challenged the 

ways of thinking

 which have allowed the industrial 

mega-racket

 [5] to gain its stranglehold on our lives.










One of these is the obsession with the idea of paid “work” – of any kind, no matter how pointless or harmful – as being an essential bulwark of everyone’s existence.




He explained: “That soul-destroying, meaningless, mechanical, monotonous, moronic work is an insult to human nature which must necessarily and inevitably produce either escapism or aggression, and that no amount of ‘bread and circuses’ can compensate for the damage done – these are facts which are neither denied nor acknowledged but are met with an unbreakable conspiracy of silence – because to deny them would be too obviously absurd and to acknowledge them would condemn the central preoccupation of modern society as a crime against humanity”. [6]




Our separation from nature is, of course, another key problem: “Modern man does not experience himself as a part of nature but as an outside force destined to dominate and destroy it”. [7]




As well as being inspired by the decentralist, degrowth economic ideas of organic radical inspirations 

Mohandas Gandhi

 [8] and 

Leopold Kohr

, [9] Schumacher was also influenced by the metaphysical critique of modernity voiced by the perennialist wing of the revived tradition.




In 

Small is Beautiful

 he quoted both 

Aldous Huxley

 [10] and 

Ananda Coomaraswamy

 [11] and he explained in 

A Guide for the Perplexed

 that he had taken the term “the Reign of Quantity” from 

René Guénon

 (

pictured

), [12] “one of the few significant metaphysicians of our time”. [13]










It was this aspect of Schumacher’s thinking which lay behind his judgement in the latter book, first published in 1977, that “while wealth may still be accumulating, the quality of man declines”. [14]




It also informed his criticism of the one-dimensionality of modern thought, in contrast to the “three-dimensional structure” of traditional wisdom. [15]




Contemporary society rejects ideas of “higher” or “lower” degrees of quality in favour of judgements based purely on quantity, he pointed out.




And yet the idea of something being “higher” is almost universally used in traditional ways of thinking across the world, he said: “‘Higher’ always means and implies ‘more inner’, ‘more interior’, ‘deeper’, ‘more intimate’; while ‘lower’ means and implies ‘more outer’, ‘more external’, ‘shallower’, ‘less intimate’. This synonymity can be found in many languages, perhaps in all of them”. [16]




It is also at the root of our ethical judgements, which regard good as being a “higher” quality than evil, argued Schumacher.




He observed: “The modern world tends to be sceptical about everything that demands man’s higher faculties. But it is not at all sceptical about scepticism, which demands hardly anything”. [17]










A Guide for the Perplexed

 is refreshingly clear about the obvious dead-end represented by the industrial monstrosity we are told is “civilization”.




Schumacher writes: “The faith in modern man’s omnipotence is wearing thin. Even if all the ‘new’ problems were solved by technological fixes, the state of futility, disorder and corruption would remain. It existed before the present crises became acute, and it will not go away by itself. More and more people are beginning to realise that ‘the modern experiment’ has failed”. [18]




Troy Southgate, whose fascinating political journey I recently 

described

, [19] takes a close look at Schumacher’s philosophy through the lens of this particular work in his 2025 book 

The World According to Fritz: E.F. Schumacher and The Perennial Philosophy

.




Obviously, there is much thematic overlap with what I wrote about, but Southgate goes into more detail in his 120 pages than I could in my profile and he does pick out some choice quotes that I wish I had used, such as Schumacher’s evocation of “the progressive constriction and narrowing of the modern mind”. [20]




He points out: “For Schumacher things have continued to decline ever since the Cartesian revolution set out to reshape man’s view of the universe.




Science Fiction

 by 

Jordan Henderson







“Logic has separated man from the great Chain of Being and, rather to seek to elevate himself to the heavens, he has fallen into a hell of his own making”. [21]




“The rationalist methodology favoured by [René] Descartes does not extend beyond the application of Reason, completely ruling out the potential of the human imagination.




“We must, he announced, even discount the information that we receive from our senses and this narrow approach to science and philosophy even suggests that whenever we encounter an intellectual barrier our investigations should cease”. [22]




Channelling Schumacher’s viewpoint, Southgate describes how Descartes (1596-1650) “became so arrogant in his efforts to overcome the great minds of the past that he portrayed both ancient and medieval philosophy as examples of congenital error”. [23]




Southgate notes that the thinker  was carrying forward the work begun by Francis Bacon (1561-1626) in launching “a scientific revolution against the established wisdom of antiquity”. [24]










As I set out in August 2025 in ‘

The Invisible College and the plan for our enslavement

‘, [25] I think both of these men were part of a deliberate effort to enact a Great Reset of those times, to undermine the foundations of European thought and culture and so pave the way for our exploitation by judeo-supremacist industrial imperialism.




Southgate describes how Schumacher regarded these changes as a “great impoverishment” in which the age-old roadmap to life had been discarded by the purveyors of a dislocated and confused world. [26]




“It is hardly surprising that we find ourselves in the middle of a tangled forest with a broken compass and no way of finding our way through the wilderness”.




He says that for Schumacher the knowledge of the past is like a network of forgotten footpaths which no longer appears on a map which has changed beyond recognition. [27]




That is very much the insight behind the organic radical project, by the way. While some of the individual thinkers featured there remain well known, what has been hidden from general view are the connections between them; the overview that making such connections can provide; the understanding that together these elements constitute 

another way of thinking

, a 

true and traditional wisdom

 which has been deliberately concealed by the modern tyranny.










Southgate writes that “the reductionist plan of the Cartesian cartographer has dispensed with the qualitative aspects of ‘higher’ and ‘lower’ features and replaced them with purely quantitative effects that offer little guidance on the voyage from A to B”. [28]




Schumacher himself declared: “The old science – ‘Wisdom’ or ‘science for understanding’ – was primarily directed ‘towards the sovereign good’, i.e. the True, the Good and the Beautiful, the knowledge of which would bring both happiness and salvation.




“The new science was directed mainly towards material power, a tendency that has meanwhile developed to such lengths that the enhancement of political and economic power is now generally taken as the first purpose of, and main justification for, expenditure on scientific work.




“The old science looked upon nature as God’s handiwork and man’s mother; the new science tends to look upon it as an adversary to be conquered or a quarry to be exploited”. [29]




From his 2020s perspective, Southgate adds: “What Schumacher calls ‘knowledge for manipulation’ has become an enormous threat and those readers who experienced the so-called pandemic of 2020 onwards will have seen how expressions such as ‘trust the science’ were designed to reinforce a global campaign of systematic disinformation”. [30]










He further cites Schumacher’s 1977 warning regarding this malevolent modern science: “If it continues to be a juggernaut outside humanistic control there will be a reaction and revulsion against it which would not exclude the possibility of violence”. [31]




And Southgate adds: “This has certainly been the case in relation to the authoritarian restrictions that were imposed during the Covid-19 debacle, not to mention similar opposition towards the scientific ‘justification’ for transgender ideology”. [32]




As well as being used to exploit and control us, this science also reduces our individual experience of life and our understanding of its meaning.




Schumacher writes: “We are given a large number of definitions of man which make him out to be nothing but an exceptionally intelligent animal with an unduly large brain, or a tool-making animal, or a political animal, or an unfinished animal, or simply a naked ape.




“No doubt, people who use these terms cheerfully include themselves in their definitions and will have some reason for doing so. Nothing is more conducive to the brutalisation of the modern world than the launching, in the name of science, of wrongful and degraded definitions of man, such as ‘the naked ape’.




“What could one expect of such a creature, of other ‘naked apes’ or, indeed, of oneself? When people speak of animals as ‘animal machines’ they soon start treating them accordingly, and when they think of people as naked apes, all doors are opened to the free entry of bestiality”. [33]










Contemporary industrial thinking drags us down into the 

lower

 level of existence which is its domain, at the same time as denying that any such thing exists.




Schumacher writes: “A person, for instance, entirely fixated in the philosophy of materialistic scientism, denying the reality of the ‘invisibles’ and confining his attention solely to what can be counted, measured and weighed, lives in a very poor world, so poor that he will experience it as a meaningless wasteland unfit for human habitation”. [34]




Modernity’s flat and fragmented analysis means people can only ever see the trees, rather than the wood, said Schumacher: “To say that life is nothing but a property of certain peculiar combinations of atoms is like saying that Shakespeare’s 

Hamlet

 is nothing but a property of a peculiar combination of letters”. [35]




Another way of putting this (

as somebody once wrote – I am not sure who now)

 is to say that it is like dismantling a TV set and scientifically concluding that there is no evidence that the programme you were watching had a plot.




Schumacher (

pictured

) condemned “a view that counts as ‘real’ only inanimate matter and treats as ‘unreal’, ‘subjective’ and therefore scientifically non-existent the invisible dimensions of life, conscioussness and self-awareness”. [36]










Half a century ago, Schumacher would not have been thinking about AI, but that certainly comes to mind when he writes that “the lower level tends to produce a kind of mimicry or counterfeit of the higher, just as an animated puppet can at times be mistaken for a living person, or a two-dimensional picture can look like three-dimensional reality”. [37]




Our task is therefore to extract ourselves from the dungeon of the lower modern industrial world and rediscover the heights which human beings are capable of achieving.




Schumacher said we need to make full use of what he called our intellectual senses, adding: “Without them, we should be unable to recognise form, pattern, regularity, harmony, rhythm and meaning, not to mention life, consciousness and self-awareness”. [38]




We also have to start to think with our hearts rather than our heads. Southgate explains that for Schumacher we can receive “flashes of understanding” that “open ‘the eye of the heart’ and allow truth to enter the soul”. [39]




“The purpose is to remove the mind from the head, where it remains constantly occupied, and redirect it to the place where body and soul converge”. [40]










“Our path, in Schumacher’s eyes, is threefold. Firstly, we must study society in light of tradition with a view to procuring a ‘temporary’ happiness’ from the external confirmation that can be gleaned.




“Secondly, this information must be thoroughly filtered so that we retain the good and discard everything that is bad. This process has been described by the Swiss psychiatrist 

Carl Gustav Jung

 (1875-1961) [41] as ‘individuation’.




“Thirdly, Schumacher says, after completing the first two steps the individual must ‘die’ to himself in the sense that personal likes and dislikes – or what he describes as ‘egocentric preoccupations’ – are considered secondary.




“Instead of being directed from outside, by external influences, one becomes 

self

-directed; this, the ultimate form of freedom is no different to being ‘God-directed'”. [42]










[1] E.F. Schumacher, 

Small is Beautiful: A Study of Economics As If People Mattered

 (London: Abacus, 1974), p. 40.

author: winter oak
title: Rallying the real anarchists!
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here




The anarchist movement of which I became part in the 1990s was very much to my liking.




It took to the streets against the globalists and their summits, it fiercely defended nature against roadbuilding and other “development” and it was defiantly opposed to the plutocratic ruling class with all its exploitation, repression and warmongering.




Anarchists expressed themselves freely, clearly, angrily and often with a sharp sense of humour.




But, progressively, all of that changed.




Opposing globalist gatherings was deemed retrograde by many, nature was increasingly regarded as a suspect reactionary construct and the emphasis shifted to “critical whiteness” and “trans rights”.




Worst of all, the joy and humour seemed to drain completely away from the movement, being replaced by the dead-eyed and narrow-minded robotic dogmatism which I had always associated with the Marxist “left”.










I began to suspect that the anarchist scene had been deliberately infiltrated and corrupted by the ruling mafia in order to disarm it as a potential source of resistance.




This was confirmed for me six or seven years ago, initially by a general anarchist failure to call out the obvious 

fakery

 of the “climate” movement and then, of course, by the appalling collaboration with the Covid manoeuvre.




I first confronted this issue in an article entitled ‘Anarchists and the Coronavirus’, published on April 3 2020, which analysed a wide range of anarchist responses to the scamdemic.




I 

wrote

: “It seems that most fellow anarchists feel obliged to respect the prevalent social taboo. They insist that they are ‘not downplaying the seriousness of the COVID-19 pandemic’ and are anxious to distance themselves from the dreaded ‘conspiracy theorists'”.




I and others had already been accused of spreading “dangerous misinformation” by anarchists who nevertheless, at this stage anyway, continued to regard us as “comrades”.




By April 26 2020 the ongoing venom directed at me by so-called “anarchists” had totally confirmed what had been a somewhat tentative conclusion.










In ‘Anarchists against freedom’, I 

warned

: “People are attaching the anarchist label, and a sort of shallow parody of anarchist ideology, to something which is not anarchism at all.




“This pseudo-anarchist thinking has not grown from anarchist philosophy and therefore can never be anything but a replica anarchism, a zombie anarchism which appears to be the real thing but lacks the anarchist soul.




“This fake anarchism is the sworn enemy of true anarchism. By stealing the body of anarchism, it banishes real anarchism from the world”.




Following this revelation, I dug deeper and in February 2021 published a 

very detailed exposé

 showing exactly how the anarchist scene had been funded and thus manipulated by globalist “philanthropists” and their 

impact investment

 industry.




I remarked: “The sterile, divisive mindset they have been spreading on behalf of their corporate paymasters should be thrown on the scrapheap of ideological history, where it belongs”.




In recent years I have often referred to my position as being 

organic radicalism

, which is a broader philosophical concept than anarchism in that it includes non-anarchist thinkers.




But I also think it is important to maintain an understanding of

 

authentic anarchism and for that purpose I have set up a new Substack called 

Real Anarchists

.




Although some of my own posts will be shared on that site, the idea is not to present my particular philosophical vision – paradoxically, real anarchism could also be regarded as broader than organic radicalism!










Instead, the goal is to restore the notion of an anarchism that can embrace a wide range of perspectives while retaining an overall fundamental coherence.




This 

openness

 is central to the very character of true anarchism, which is not a set dogma but more like an 

existential attitude

 and it is this 

essence

 of anarchism which I seek to uphold.




I know full well that, historically, anarchism has not always reflected all my own beliefs – a blind faith in “science” and “progress” was very prevalent for a long time, for instance, and my interest in cultural rootedness is no doubt not shared by those anarchists who champion an internationalism that is hardly distinguishable from globalism.




But I would counter that anarchism is necessarily a call for decentralisation, not just down from the national-state level but down from that of the so-called “international community” and all its centralising infrastructure.




And if anarchists believe that societies can function perfectly well without government, that can 

only be

 because of the natural order that reigns in small and cohesive human communities.










The new blog will present both historical and contemporary anarchist content – I am not sure how it will evolve over time and I welcome any suggestions, submissions or constructive comments.




The aim is a long-term one and is not about creating some kind of new movement going by the name of “real anarchism”.




Indeed, success for the project would be that the “real” part of the term becomes redundant, because everyone now understands what actual anarchism is and is not.




The idea is to help conjure back into life the lost anarchist soul!
